prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Out of scope: grid, port. Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment); Main Transformer (site-specific trip); export cable→Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; applies Dispatcher ceiling); Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Relay. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss; shutdown on confirmed fire), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss; no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby, Turbine Lockout (no remote restart during fire investigation). Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms: safety>protection>export; not cleared on detector reset. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; data→Shore Control Room; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway). Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; hub; holds last limit on grid comms loss). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale). Operations Radio Console (voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft). Personnel Tracking Console (route entry/exit records). Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. HSE Officer: evacuation advice. Field Supervisor: work status→Shore Control Room. North Access Scanner: credential/period/area check; deny otherwise; gate secured if unverifiable; no verbal override; unique transaction ID. Southern route scanner: individual credential, area/time authorization; timestamped logs; barrier closed on failure; anti-tailgating; escorts verified; faults→out of service; alternative entry; credential-free emergency egress. East Service Lift: interlock/overload checks; hoist/cable inspection; Electrical Technician checks supply faults; Field Supervisor records inspection in maintenance system, confirms no exposure to loads, communicates/records

New part:
S889: The west route landing doors are inspected for damage, secure closure, and unobstructed movement.
S890: The operator confirms that the car floor is level with the boarding landing before permitting entry or exit.
S891: Lighting inside the car and at each landing must be adequate for safe movement and inspection.
S892: The operator checks that the controls respond correctly and that the emergency stop is accessible.
S893: Door interlocks and other protective devices must be functional before the lift is placed in service.
S894: Protective devices must not be bypassed to maintain access or avoid delay.
S895: The operator confirms that the expected load, including tools and carried equipment, remains within the rated capacity.
S896: Passengers distribute themselves and their equipment to avoid obstructing the doors or control panel.
S897: Loose tools and materials are secured against movement during travel.
S898: The operator confirms that all occupants are ready and that the doors are fully closed before starting movement.
S899: During travel, occupants remain inside the car and avoid interfering with the controls or doors.
S900: The operator monitors lift movement for unusual noise, vibration, hesitation, or irregular stopping.
S901: Any unexpected movement or control response requires the operator to stop the lift at the nearest safe landing when practicable.
S902: If the car stops between landings, occupants use the designated alarm or communication method and remain inside the car.
S903: Personnel do not attempt to open doors or climb out of a stopped car without direction from the response team.
S904: At the destination, the operator confirms that the car is level and stationary before opening the doors.
S905: Occupants exit without crowding, and the operator checks that tools and equipment have been removed from the car.
S906: The Field Supervisor ensures that the lift is left secure and that any irregularity is reported through the established site process.
S907: The West Service Lift is removed from service if a condition could compromise safe movement, pending assessment and corrective action.
S908: The system measures operational performance against approved service objectives and documented fleet baselines.
S909: Availability is reported for each turbine and for the fleet, with planned maintenance and forced outages classified separately.
S910: Energy production measures include delivered energy, production lost during downtime, and the duration of grid-related restrictions.
S911: Maintenance performance is assessed through work completion time, repeat work, overdue tasks, and the proportion of work completed as planned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
